tasks.title: Audit and harden an adversarial benchmark verifier
tasks.objective: Audit an adversarial benchmark evaluation stack for grader compromise, answer leakage, evidence forgery, custody failures, false accepts, false rejects and benchmark-version drift. Distinguish invalid evidence from a genuinely failing candidate, and require an independent pristine regrade.
tasks.agent_prompt: Inspect the public design-only CEB benchmark-integrity corpus and produce a threat-to-control traceability plan. For each negative and positive control, identify the protected asset, trust boundary, expected qualification decision, required evidence and unresolved dependency. Do not execute candidate code, grader code, attack payloads or task-controlled scripts. Do not modify the evaluator or weaken a gate. Keep task-resolution outcomes separate from evidence qualification.

split.freshness_policy: Design-only. Future executable variants must use independently authored verifier attack cases and preserve sealed holdouts.

notes: Design-only benchmark-integrity task. The machine-readable scenario catalog is benchmarks/ceb/integrity/attack-catalog.v0.json.
The initial catalog contains 28 negative/adversarial controls and 8 positive/valid-state controls; all are unexecuted scenario definitions.
False-accept and false-reject rates must be reported separately with raw denominators and uncertainty; critical false accepts are hard qualification failures.
A valid receipt for an incorrect candidate is a legitimate candidate failure, not a verifier false reject. Evidence qualification and candidate correctness are separate axes.
No performance score is produced by writing or reviewing this design record. Keep it out of all agent task-resolution aggregates.

Do not execute task-controlled code or attack payloads until OS-level isolation is independently qualified under issue #10064; signer custody and failure-domain independence remain tracked under #10369.

tasks.title: Construct a typed repository twin and predict change impact
tasks.objective: Inspect a pinned multi-crate Rust workspace and construct an exact, versioned graph of packages, modules, symbols, types, calls, trait implementations, feature gates, build targets and tests. Predict the change impact of specified source/configuration edits, then update the graph after incremental invalidation without retaining stale facts.
tasks.agent_prompt: Build a machine-readable typed repository graph from the supplied source and manifest snapshot. For each requested edit, identify affected symbols, call sites, trait implementations, features, build targets and tests with evidence spans. After a sequence of file/configuration edits, incrementally refresh the graph and report removed, changed and newly introduced facts. Do not execute repository build scripts, tests or generated code; use the provided static source and manifest fixture only.

split.freshness_policy: Design-only. Use a synthetic repository family for development and keep repository-family-disjoint holdout fixtures for qualification.

notes: A five-crate static synthetic workspace, fixture-declared gold graph and seven deterministic edit scenarios are committed under benchmarks/ceb/fixtures/repository-twin-synthetic-v0/.

The initial graph contains 32 nodes and 37 expected edges, with a verified one-line source declaration anchor for every node. Expected semantic edges are explicitly not compiler-verified; no independent compiler/rust-analyzer receipt exists.
The fixture has not been compiled or executed. Its source tree digest, pinned environment, reference grader and hidden labels are not provisioned; the task must remain design_only.
Gold labels separate syntax-declared facts, manifest-declared feature/target edges and expected semantic relationships.
Evaluate retrieval and change-impact precision/recall independently; do not count inferred links as compiler-resolved truth.
